llm.summary: This Etsy category lookup skill is not clearly dangerous, but it sends API-key-authenticated queries to a remote LinkFox service and stores full responses locally despite describing the lookup as local.

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is Etsy category lookup, which fits the script name and API endpoint, but the user-facing description says it searches a locally synced Etsy category library while the script always calls a remote LinkFox gateway for uncached lookups.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The trigger text is broad and instructs activation even when the tool name is not mentioned, based on an inferred local category-ID lookup; that is under-scoped given the actual network call and credential use.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The artifact contains a markdown skill, one Python standard-library script, and an API reference; there are no package-install hooks, auto-run install steps, or hidden binaries.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Remote access is plausible for a third-party category service, but the script sends the API key plus SESSION_ID, MODE_ID, and APP_NAME headers, and allows the gateway host to be changed through LINKFOX_TOOL_GATEWAY without allowlisting.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The script writes full API responses and cache files by default under linkfox paths, with fallback to the home directory or temp directory if preferred paths are unavailable; this persistence is only partly disclosed and is broader than a simple lookup utility needs.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Review before installing. Use this only if you are comfortable sending Etsy category search terms and LinkFox authorization headers to LinkFox’s gateway. Avoid setting LINKFOX_TOOL_GATEWAY unless you fully trust the destination, and expect full responses to be written under local linkfox directories unless you run with cache/storage controls.
llm.findings:
[TT3] unexpected: Accepted as a material concern: the code constructs a POST request using an environment-selected gateway and includes the LinkFox API key and session metadata in headers, which is overbroad for a category lookup unless the host is constrained.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Accepted: the script persists complete responses and cache data by default, while the top-level skill description does not clearly tell users that lookup results will be stored locally.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Accepted: the documentation frames the data as locally synced category lookup, but the implementation performs remote API requests to the LinkFox gateway for uncached searches.
[SQP-1] unexpected: Accepted: broad auto-activation is not proportionate when use can transmit queries and credentials to a remote service.
[SQP-3] expected: Downgraded: the Chinese-only wording is a usability and transparency issue, but it is not by itself a security concern.
